dataset.name: US Live Poker Room Rake Caps And Bad Beat Jackpot Benchmark Report
dataset.description: Analysis Of 324+ Verified US Commercial Casinos, Tribal Gaming Properties, And Regulated Card Rooms Shows Standard $1/$2 And $1/$3 No-Limit Hold'em Cash Games Charge A 10% Pot Rake Capped At $5 To $7 Plus A $1 To $2 Promotional Jackpot Drop.
keywords: US Live Poker Room Rake And Jackpot Benchmark

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: US Live Poker Room Rake And Jackpot Benchmark Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Low-Stakes No-Limit Hold'em ($1/$2 And $1/$3) Operates On A 10% Percentage Rake Capped Between $5 And $7 In 84% Of Surveyed US Commercial And Tribal Card Rooms.

variableMeasured.name: US Live Poker Room Rake And Jackpot Benchmark Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Promotional Drops For Bad Beat Jackpots And High-Hand Promotions Average $1 To $2 Per Qualifying Pot Reaching A Flop.

variableMeasured.name: US Live Poker Room Rake And Jackpot Benchmark Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Mid-To-High Stakes ($2/$5 And $5/$10+ NLH And PLO) Increasingly Transition To Half-Hour Seat Time Charges ($6 To $9 Per 30-Minute Down) Which Reduce Effective Hourly Player Cost Relative To Per-Pot Rake.

variableMeasured.name: US Live Poker Room Rake And Jackpot Benchmark Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: Texas And Oregon Social Membership Clubs Utilize Time-Based Seat Rentals And Club Membership Models With Zero Per-Hand Pot Rake.

dataset.name: Daily Live Poker Tournament Buy-In, Rake, And Guarantee Index
dataset.description: Audit Of 4,500+ Weekly Recurring Live Poker Tournaments Across North America Reveals A Median Entry Buy-In Of $140, A Median House Plus Staff Fee Allocation Of 21.4% In Sub-$200 Daily Events, And Significantly Lower Fee Ratios (12% To 16%) In Weekend Deepstack Events Above $300.
keywords: Daily Poker Tournament Buy-In And Guarantee Index

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: Daily Poker Tournament Buy-In And Guarantee Index Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Sub-$100 Daily Morning And Nightly Turbo Tournaments Carry The Highest Effective Fee Percentage (22% To 28% Combined House And Staff Allocation) Due To Fixed Dealer And Floor Overhead.

variableMeasured.name: Daily Poker Tournament Buy-In And Guarantee Index Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Mid-Tier Daily Events ($125 To $250 Buy-In) Represent 54% Of All Scheduled Weekly Tournaments With 20-Minute To 30-Minute Blind Levels And 20,000 To 30,000 Starting Chips.

variableMeasured.name: Daily Poker Tournament Buy-In And Guarantee Index Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Weekend Deepstack And Multi-Flight Events ($300 To $600 Buy-In) Offer The Highest Structural Value With 13% To 16% Total Fee Deductions And 30-Minute To 40-Minute Blind Levels.

variableMeasured.name: Daily Poker Tournament Buy-In And Guarantee Index Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: Zero-Entry Free-To-Play Online Tournaments On Smarter.Poker Award $2,000 Daily With 0% Entry Rake And Zero Deposit Requirements.

dataset.name: GTO Solver Equilibrium Vs. Population Leak Frequency Study
dataset.description: Comparison Of 100BB 6-Max Game Theory Optimal (GTO) Equilibrium Baselines Against Recreational And Low-Stakes Population Tendencies Identifies Five Systematic EV Leaks: Under-3-Betting Suited Wheel Bluffs, Over-Calling 3-Bets Out Of Position, Over-C-Betting Multiway Flops, Under-Bluffing Turn Check-Raises, And Under-Folding To River Overbets.
keywords: GTO Solver Vs. Population Leak Study

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: GTO Solver Vs. Population Leak Study Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Preflop Cold-Calling: Low-Stakes Populations Cold-Call 2-Bets From Middle Position And Cutoff At 14% To 19% Frequency, Whereas Rake-Adjusted 100BB Solver Baselines Play Near-Pure 3-Bet-Or-Fold From Non-Button/Big-Blind Seats.

variableMeasured.name: GTO Solver Vs. Population Leak Study Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Big Blind Defense Vs. Steals: Recreational Players Under-Defend Suited Connected And Wheel Combinations Against 2.2x Button Opens While Over-Defending Dominated Offsuit Broadways.

variableMeasured.name: GTO Solver Vs. Population Leak Study Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Turn Barrel Frequencies: After Continuation Betting Flop, Population Turn Follow-Through Drops Below 38% On Scare-Card Runouts, Allowing Aggressive Floaters To Realize Excess Equity.

variableMeasured.name: GTO Solver Vs. Population Leak Study Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: River Overbet Response: Population Bluff-Frequency On 125%+ Pot River Overbets In Low-Stakes Games Remains Below The 35.7% Minimum Bluff Threshold, Making Exploitative Over-Folding With One-Pair Bluff-Catchers High-EV.

dataset.name: US Casino Poker Dealer Toke Rate, Down Duration, And Hourly Earnings Benchmark
dataset.description: Empirical Analysis Of Live Casino And Cardroom Dealer Rotations Shows Standard 30-Minute Dealer Downs Yield An Average Of 13 To 17 Hands Dealt In No-Limit Hold'em, With Cash Game Toke Averages Ranging From $12 To $24 Per 30-Minute Down ($24 To $48+ Per Dealing Hour Before Base Wage) Depending On Region, Stake, And Table Shorthandedness.
keywords: US Poker Dealer Toke Rate And Earnings Benchmark

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Dealer Toke Rate And Earnings Benchmark Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Down Cadence Standard: 92% Of Surveyed US Poker Rooms Operate On A 30-Minute Table Down With A 30-Minute To 90-Minute String Rotation Followed By A 20-Minute To 30-Minute Break.

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Dealer Toke Rate And Earnings Benchmark Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Cash Vs. Tournament Down Variance: Cash Game Downs Generate Immediate Per-Pot Tokes Averaging $12 To $22 Per Down At $1/$2 And $1/$3, Whereas Daily Tournament Downs Pool A 3% To 7% Staff Appreciation Allocation Paid Via Per-Down Point Shares.

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Dealer Toke Rate And Earnings Benchmark Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Plo And High-Hand Impact: Pot-Limit Omaha And Active High-Hand Promotion Tables Increase Hands-Induced Pot Size, Raising Average Toke Per Down By 18% To 30% Over Equivalent Hold'em Tables.

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Dealer Toke Rate And Earnings Benchmark Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: IRS Tax Compliance: Accurate Daily Logging Of Cash Tokes, Tournament Down Shares, Base Hourly Wages, And Gaming License Renewals Reduces Year-End Audit Friction For Professional Dealers.

dataset.name: Tournament ICM Bubble Factor, Risk Premium, And Final Table Equity Study
dataset.description: Malmuth-Harville Independent Chip Model (ICM) Evaluations Across Standard Top-15% MTT Payout Structures Demonstrate That Medium Stacks Facing Chip Leaders On The Direct Money Bubble And Final Table Pay Jumps Incur Risk Premiums Of +12% To +24%, Requiring 62% To 74% Raw All-In Equity Where Chip-EV Requires Only 50%.
keywords: Tournament ICM Bubble Factor And Risk Premium Study

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: Tournament ICM Bubble Factor And Risk Premium Study Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Asymmetric Chip Value: In Tournament Play, Doubling A Average Stack At A 9-Handed Final Table Increases Dollar Equity ($EV) By Only 55% To 68% Of The Original Stack Value, While Losing The Stack Costs 100% Of Remaining $EV.

variableMeasured.name: Tournament ICM Bubble Factor And Risk Premium Study Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Medium-Stack Paralyzation: When Two Short Stacks (<10BB) Are Present At A Final Table, A 30BB Medium Stack Calling A 60BB Chip Leader All-In Faces A Bubble Factor Between 1.65 And 2.20 (+15% To +23% Risk Premium).

variableMeasured.name: Tournament ICM Bubble Factor And Risk Premium Study Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Chip Leader Aggression Leverage: Big Stacks Covering The Table Experience Bubble Factors Below 1.15 Against Medium Stacks, Allowing Profitable Wide Open-Shoves And 3-Bet Jams With Suited Connectors And Blockers.

variableMeasured.name: Tournament ICM Bubble Factor And Risk Premium Study Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: Final Table Deal Negotiations: ICM Chop Calculations Frequently Award 8% To 14% More Prize Pool Equity To Short-And-Medium Stacks Than Chip-Chop Proportions.

dataset.name: Pot-Limit Omaha (PLO4, PLO5, PLO6) Multiway Equity Compression And Bankroll Variance Study
dataset.description: Monte Carlo Evaluations Across 100,000+ Simulated Runouts Show Preflop Equity Edges Compress Dramatically From No-Limit Hold'em (AA Vs. Random: 85.2%) To 4-Card PLO (AAKK Double-Suited Vs. Random: 68.8%), 5-Card PLO (64.2%), And 6-Card PLO (60.8%), Requiring 60 To 150 Buy-In Bankrolls To Maintain Sub-5% Risk Of Ruin.
keywords: PLO4, PLO5, And PLO6 Equity And Variance Study

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: PLO4, PLO5, And PLO6 Equity And Variance Study Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Preflop Equity Compression: In 4-Card PLO, Even The Absolute Best Starting Hand (A-A-K-K Double-Suited) Is Only A 53.6% To 46.4% Favorite Against A Connected Rundown Like J-T-9-8 Double-Suited.

variableMeasured.name: PLO4, PLO5, And PLO6 Equity And Variance Study Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: 5-Card And 6-Card PLO Nut Requirement: Adding A Fifth And Sixth Hole Card Increases Postflop Flush And Full-House Frequencies By 42% And 78% Respectively, Rendering Non-Nut Flushes And Unimproved Sets Negative-EV Stack-Offs In Multiway Pots.

variableMeasured.name: PLO4, PLO5, And PLO6 Equity And Variance Study Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Standard Deviation Escalation: Typical 100-Hand Standard Deviation Rises From 65-85 BB/100 In Live NLH To 120-145 BB/100 In PLO4 And 160-210 BB/100 In PLO5/PLO6.

variableMeasured.name: PLO4, PLO5, And PLO6 Equity And Variance Study Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: Bankroll Multiplier Guidelines: A Winning Player At 5 BB/100 Requires ~30 Buy-Ins For Sub-5% Risk Of Ruin In NLH, ~75 Buy-Ins In PLO4, And 120+ Buy-Ins In PLO5 And PLO6.

dataset.name: US Poker Player IRS Form W-2G Thresholds, Session Accounting, And Tax Deductibility Benchmark
dataset.description: Analysis Of US Federal Tax Reporting Rules And Contemporaneous Poker Session Logs Shows That Casino Poker Tournaments Trigger Mandatory IRS Form W-2G Reporting When Net Winnings (Prize Minus Buy-In) Exceed $5,000, And That Session-Level Netting Reduces Taxable Gross Income Liability Compared To Unlogged Cage Cashouts.
keywords: US Poker Tax W-2G And Session Accounting Benchmark

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Tax W-2G And Session Accounting Benchmark Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Form W-2G Tournament Threshold: US Casinos Issue Form W-2G For Poker Tournaments When The Payout Minus The Buy-In Exceeds $5,000, With 24% Mandatory Federal Backup Withholding Applied If A Valid TIN/SSN Is Not Provided.

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Tax W-2G And Session Accounting Benchmark Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Cash Game vs. Tournament Reporting: Standard Live Cash Games Do Not Trigger Form W-2G Regardless Of Cashout Size, Though Cash Transactions Exceeding $10,000 In A Single Gaming Day Require FinCEN Currency Transaction Report (CTR) Filing.

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Tax W-2G And Session Accounting Benchmark Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Contemporaneous Session Log Requirement: Under IRS Revenue Procedure 77-29, Players Must Record Date, Casino Location, Game Type, Buy-In, Cashout, And Net Win/Loss Per Session Rather Than Netting A Full Year In A Single Lump Sum.

variableMeasured.name: US Poker Tax W-2G And Session Accounting Benchmark Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: Winning vs. Losing Session Separation: Recreational Filers Report Gross Winning Sessions On Form 1040 Schedule 1 And Deduct Losing Sessions Only Up To Winning Sessions On Schedule A (Itemized Deductions), Making Accurate Session Boundaries Critical.

variableMeasured.description: Seat Vacancy Reduction: Automated Two-Way SMS Seat Alerts Cut Average Empty-Seat Duration From 11.4 Minutes (Manual PA Paging) To 4.1 Minutes.

variableMeasured.description: Call-In Conversion Rate: Remote Mobile Waitlist Check-Ins With 60-Minute Arrival Windows Convert To Seated Players At 78.6%, Compared To 54.2% For Unverified Phone Call-Ins.

variableMeasured.description: Must-Move And Table-Balancing Efficiency: Automated Must-Move Queue Tracking Reduces Short-Handed Table Break Rates By 31% During Late-Night Off-Peak Hours.

dataset.name: 2026 Mystery Bounty Vs. Progressive Knockout (PKO) EV & Bounty Power Factor Study
dataset.description: Comparative Monte Carlo And Bounty Power Factor Analysis Of Progressive Knockout (PKO) Versus Mystery Bounty Tournaments Shows That While PKO Events Award 25% Of Starting Buy-In Immediately Upon Each Elimination From Hand One, Mystery Bounty Envelopes Activate Exclusively At Day 2 Or In-The-Money (ITM), Causing Chip-Stack Utility On The Mystery Activation Bubble To Surge By 38% To 64% Relative To Standard Freezeout ICM.
keywords: Mystery Bounty Vs. PKO EV And Power Factor

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: Mystery Bounty Vs. PKO EV And Power Factor Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Early-Stage Chip Accumulation Imperative: Because Mystery Bounties Cannot Be Won Until Day 2 Or ITM, Early-Level Eliminations Yield Zero Immediate Bounty Cash, Making Chip Accumulation To Cover The Field At Activation The Primary Strategic Objective.

variableMeasured.name: Mystery Bounty Vs. PKO EV And Power Factor Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: PKO Starting Bounty Conversion: In A 50% Bounty Pool PKO, Each Starting Bounty Equals 25% Of A Starting Stack In Immediate Cash Plus 25% Added To The Winner's Head, Reducing Required Heads-Up All-In Calling Equity By 8.3% At Equal Stacks.

variableMeasured.name: Mystery Bounty Vs. PKO EV And Power Factor Finding 3
variableMeasured.description: Mystery Activation Bubble Distortion: When Mystery Envelopes Activate At 12% To 15% Of The Field Remaining, Covering Stacks Experience Negative Risk Premiums Against Short Stacks (-12% To -19% Equity Discount), Whereas Covered Stacks Face Severe Survival Penalties.

variableMeasured.name: Mystery Bounty Vs. PKO EV And Power Factor Finding 4
variableMeasured.description: Top-Envelope Removal Decay: Once The Top 1% And 2% Jackpot Envelopes Are Drawn From A Mystery Drum, Remaining Average Envelope EV Drops By 28% To 44%, Requiring Immediate Tightening Of Wide Bounty-Hunting Calling Ranges.

dataset.name: 2026 Short Deck (6+ Hold'em) All-In Equity & Button-Ante Mathematical Benchmark
dataset.description: Exact Combinatorial Evaluation Of The 36-Card Short Deck (6+ Hold'em) Format Demonstrates That Removing Ranks 2 Through 5 Compresses Preflop All-In Equities By 11% To 18% Compared To 52-Card Texas Hold'em, Makes Flushes Significantly Rarer Than Full Houses (1.96% Vs. 3.26% On 7-Card Boards), And Elevates Open-Ended Straight Draws To A 48.5% Flop-To-River Completion Rate.
keywords: Short Deck 6+ Hold'em Equity And Ante Math

includedInDataCatalog.name: Smarter.Poker Open Quantitative Poker & Live Cardroom Data Catalog

variableMeasured.name: Short Deck 6+ Hold'em Equity And Ante Math Finding 1
variableMeasured.description: Flush Over Full House Ranking Proof: In A 36-Card Deck With Only 9 Cards Per Suit, Completing A 5-Card Flush By The River Occurs On Just 1.96% Of 7-Card Deals Compared To 3.26% For A Full House Or Quads, Justifying Flush Beating Full House.

variableMeasured.name: Short Deck 6+ Hold'em Equity And Ante Math Finding 2
variableMeasured.description: Rule Of 3 And 6 For Out Counting: Because Only 31 Unseen Cards Remain On The Flop (And 30 On The Turn), Each Clean Out Provides ~3.2% Equity On The Turn And ~6.3% Flop-To-River, Giving An 8-Out Straight Draw ~48.5% Equity Against Top Pair.
